The appellant/accused Shyam Singh has preferred the present appeal, being aggrieved by the judgment dated 28.09.2018 and order on sentence dated 26.03.2019 passed by Ms. Neeti Suri Mishra, the then Ld. MM, Central District, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi (the trial court) whereby the appellant was held guilty and convicted for the offences under sections 468/120-B IPC and 471 IPC and was sentenced to undergo Simple Imprisonment (SI) for five months for the offence u/s 120B IPC for criminal conspiracy for cheating complainant, further SI of five months for the offence u/s 120B IPC for conspiracy to forge the documents, further SI for three years for the offence u/s 468 IPC and lastly SI for two years for the offence u/s 471 IPC.

3. The facts in brief leading to the present case are that in the year 1997, the complainant was desirous of purchasing a plot of land.

In October, 1997, he was approached by co-accused Ram Pal Shyam Singh vs State on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119749099/

sentences.text: He also told the complainant that the plot was registered in the name of one of his acquaintances namely co-accused Nanak Chand and was his benami property.
All the negotiations with respect to the sale/purchase of the said plot was done by accused Ram Pal, who visited the complainant several times for the said purpose.

After negotiations, the complainant purchased the said plot for a sum of Rs.1,30,000/- vide three sale deeds, all dated 12.11.1997 and duly registered with the office of Sub-Registrar, Kashmere Gate, on 24.11.1997 from co-accused Nanak Chand, who was also friend of accused Ram Pal.

Subsequently, the complainant found that he had been cheated by accused Nanak Chand, Ram Pal Singh and others, as the said Nanak Chand had executed the aforesaid sale deeds in criminal conspiracy with each other since,
the said plot was not owned by Nanak Chand but rather it was in the name of a partnership firm known as M/s Sachdeva Industries.

sentences.text: Upon local enquiry, the complainant found that the accused persons namely Ram Pal Singh and Nanak Chand had shown him forged sale documents of the plot of land purportedly executed by one Joginder Singh and one Munshi Ram in favour of accused Nanak Chand, whereas the persons who had signed the sale documents had impersonated themselves as Joginder Singh and Munshi Ram for the purpose of preparation of forged documents.

Complainant later on, also came to know that Joginder Singh and Munshi Ram were joint owners of the said plot which was in the name of M/s Sachdeva Industries and after death of Munshi Ram, his son O.P. Sachdeva had become joint owner alongwith Joginder Singh.

Sh. O.P. Sachdeva, the son of Munshi Ram also informed the complainant that the photographs on the photocopy of GPA were not that of actual Joginder Singh and Munshi Ram and the said Joginder Singh and Munshi Ram had also not sold the plot to anyone.
Moreover, the said Munshi Ram had already expired about 12 years ago so even otherwise, he could not have executed GPA dated 07.11.1997 in favour of Nanak Chand.
Accordingly, the complainant got the present FIR registered.

During investigation, the role of many other accused persons including appellant/accused herein was revealed who in criminal conspiracy with each other, had forged the sale documents of the plot purportedly in favour of Nanak Chand, which was later on used to cheat the complainant by making false representation that Nanak Chand had purchased the property from its real owners.

Investigation was completed and chargesheet was filed before Ld.
MM.
5.

sentences.text: During trial, two more accused persons namely Nanak Chand and Ram Pal Singh also expired and hence, the matter thereafter proceeded only against the appellant/accused Shyam Singh.
6. After completion of trial, the appellant/accused was convicted for the offences u/s 120B/468 IPC and 471 IPC and sentenced as aforesaid.

In the judgment dated 28.09.2018, the Ld. MM has held that since criminal conspiracies are hatched in secrecy, there is seldom any direct evidence of it, by relying upon several judicial pronouncements.

It was held that the execution of sale documents by Munshi Ram in favour of co-accused Nanak Chand on 07.11.1997 was impossible since Munshi Ram had expired 12 years ago which was proved through his death certificate Ex. PW-2/N.

Though, there was no direct evidence regarding criminal conspiracy between the accused persons but from the testimony of PW-2, it was proved that the appellant/ accused had executed forged sale documents dated 07.11.1997 by impersonating himself either as Munshi Ram or Joginder Singh.

As regards the offence u/s 468/471 IPC is concerned, the Ld. Trial Court while relying upon the testimony of PW-1,
PW-3 and PW-6 opined that the allegations of forgery against appellant/accused Shyam Singh was proved relating to sale documents dated 07.11.1997 Ex. P-4 to Ex. P-7. PW-6 the document writer,
had deposed before the court that appellant/accused Shyam Singh had appeared before him and appended his signature upon the documents as Joginder Singh which shows that not only he impersonated himself as Joginder Singh but also dishonestly made and signed the concerned documents with the intention to cause him to believe that they were being made by actual Joginder Singh (owner of the plot in question) despite the fact that he was impersonating as Joginder Singh.

Other evidence against the appellant/accused was also considered and the court was of the opinion that the offences u/s 120B/468 and 471 IPC were duly proved against the appellant/accused and he was accordingly convicted.

sentences.text: The crux of allegations against the appellant/accused is that he had entered into a criminal conspiracy with other accused persons whereby a forged GPA dated 07.11.1997 Ex. P-4, forged receipt dated 07.11.1997 Ex. P-5, forged Agreement to sell dated 07.11.1997 Ex. P-6, forged affidavit dated 07.11.1997 Ex. P-7 were prepared by them wherein two of the accused persons impersonated themselves as Joginder Singh and Munshi Ram respectively (the executant owners of plot in question) before the Sub-Registrar, Kashmere Gate and also signed the aforesaid documents as executants Joginder Singh and Munshi Ram despite being completely different persons.
The appellant/ accused is alleged to have signed the aforesaid documents as Joginder Singh s/o Ram Lal.

16. The fact that documents Ex. P-4 to P-7 are forged and fabricated documents is beyond shadow of doubt since, it has come on record that Munshi Ram s/o Kashi Ram had already expired on 23.05.1989 as reflected from his death certificate Ex. PW-2/N i.e. 8 years before the execution of these documents.
Hence, there was no question that he could have signed documents on 07.11.1997 or could have appeared before the Sub Registrar later on for registration of those documents.

Even as regards, the signatures of Joginder Singh on those documents are concerned, it has been proved that they are not the signatures of Joginder Singh and in fact, Joginder Singh has been examined as PW-1 in the present case, DOD : 04.01.2023 Page no. 7 of 14 Shyam Singh vs State CA No. 219//19 who denied that signatures on those documents were his or that he had ever sold the plot in question to anyone.

sentences.text: The signatures on those documents were not of that Joginder Singh were also proved from the fact that the specimen signatures of actual Joginder Singh examined as PW-1 were taken by the IO vide Ex. PW-1/A and Ex. PW-1/B and sent to FSL and as per the report of FSL expert Ex. PW- 16/A, the signatures on the forged documents were not that of actual Joginder Singh.
So it is beyond doubt that documents Ex. P-4 to P-7 are forged documents as its executants had impersonated themselves to be the actual owners of the plot.

17. As far as evidence against the appellant/accused is concerned, both PW-2 and PW-3 have stated that the appellant/accused had signed the above documents Ex. P-4 to P-7 either as Joginder Singh or Munshi Ram.

It has been rightly contended on behalf of appellant/accused that both the witnesses could not pin point whether accused/appellant had signed on those documents as Joginder Singh or as Munshi Ram and have not specifically alleged that appellant/accused had signed as Joginder Singh.

In fact, it would be appropriate to say that the testimony of PW-2 is irrelevant as far as proving the signatures on those documents are concerned since, PW-2 was neither present at the time when documents Ex. P-4 to P-7 were executed or got registered nor he was familiar with the signatures of Joginder Singh or Munshi Ram or the witnesses to those documents or even the signatures of accused persons herein, including appellant/accused.
The knowledge of PW2 qua the signatures on Ex. P-4 to Ex.P- 7 is merely based on the information which he gathered from his local inquiry and not within his personal knowledge.
18. However, in this regard, the testimony of PW-3 i.e. the then Sub- Registrar, Kashmere Gate is quite relevant.

Though, he could not tell the court DOD : 04.01.2023 Page no. 8 of 14 Shyam Singh vs State CA No. 219//19 whether the appellant/accused had signed the above documents either as Joginder Singh or as Munshi Ram but he did depose before the court that the appellant/accused had appeared before him at the time of execution of those documents.

sentences.text: It is worth mentioning that the appellant/accused had not denied anywhere that the photographs on the documents Ex. P-4 to P-7 were not that of him, rather he has levelled the allegation on co-accused Shiv Charan stating that Shiv Charan had misused his photographs in conspiracy with other co-accused persons.

It is also pertinent to mention that in the capacity of Sub-Registrar, the concerned authority, carries out registration of hundreds and thousands of documents during his tenure and it is quite impossible for him to remember each and every such person appearing before him by face and he can only depose on the basis of the record, which he did so in the present case.
Moreover, there is nothing to discard the testimony of this witness.

So it does prove that appellant/accused did appear before PW3 at the time of registration of those forged documents Ex. P-4 to P-7.
19.

The fact that the appellant/accused had signed as Joginder Singh on the above documents is however proved from the testimony of PW-6, who deposed before the court that he was doing job of typist outside the old court of Kashmere Gate.

He further deposed that one Phool Kumar (since discharged) who was his neighbour, used to come to his office for preparation of GPA documents and the said Phool Kumar had provided him the particulars of both the parties and particulars of the property in question of this case, for which the documents were to be prepared.
The name of the first party on the documents was Munshi Ram and Joginder Singh and the name of second party was Nanak Chand.
After preparation of the documents i.e. GPA, agreement to Sell, etc., he had handed over the same to Phool Kumar.

The signatures of both the parties were obtained DOD : 04.01.2023 Page no. 9 of 14 Shyam Singh vs State CA No. 219//19 on the documents and he had produced the said documents before Sub Registrar alongwith the said Phool Kumar.

sentences.text: Thereafter, PW6 had specifically pointed out towards appellant/accused Shyam Singh by stating that accused Shyam Singh had appended his signature as Joginder Singh.

This witness has not at all been cross- examined by the accused persons including the appellant/accused and so, the testimony of this witness has remained unrebutted and will be read against the appellant/accused.

20. The factum of appellant/accused signing the above documents as Joginder Singh is also corroborated from the testimony of appellant/ accused who was examined as DW-2 as he had himself stated that co-accused Shiv Charan had come to him and stated that he wanted to sell a plot which was in the name of his friend and he (DW2) had agreed to be a witness in the sale documents.

Though, appellant/accused as DW2 had stated that he had carefully read over the documents and did not find anywhere in the said documents that he was the owner of the said plot, but rather his name appeared on those documents as witness with the name of Shyam Singh, so he signed those documents as witness.
Thereafter, Shiv Charan took all the documents from him and went away.

Since, the appellant/accused could not specify which documents he had signed and for which plot,
so his vague defence rather goes against him.

This is rather a tacit/indirect admission of appellant/accused that the documents which he referred in his testimony were the same documents Ex.P-4 to Ex.P-7 and he had signed them at the instance of Shiv Charan, who is also signatory to documents Ex. P-4 to P-7 21.

P-4 to P-7.

So, even as per the FSL opinion, appellant/accused had himself signed as Joginder Singh on documents Ex. P-4 to P-7.
22.

Hence, in view of the aforesaid, it is clearly proved that the appellant/accused had participated in forgery of the above documents by signing the same as Joginder Singh for the purpose of cheating and so offence u/s 468 IPC is duly proved against him.
23. As regards, criminal conspiracy is concerned, the same is writ large on the face of it.

Two persons impersonate themselves as the actual owners of one plot, out of which the appellant/accused impersonated as Joginder Singh and another co-accused Shiv Charan (since expired) impersonated himself as Munshi Ram (already expired 8 years ago from the date of execution of the documents Ex. P-4 to P-7) and they then executed GPA, Agreement to Sell, etc in favour of other co-accused Nanak Chand and even got it registered from the office of Sub- Registrar.
These forged documents were then used by co-accused Rampal Singh to cheat the complainant for inducing him to purchase the plot without having ownership rights on it.
This was not possible until and unless there was a prior meeting of minds of the accused persons and them having hatched a criminal conspiracy to cheat the complainant.

Infact the sale deeds in favor of complainant Ex. P-1 to P-3 were executed within 15 days of the preparation of forged DOD : 04.01.2023 Page no. 11 of 14 Shyam Singh vs State CA No. 219//19 documents Ex. P-4 to Ex. P-7 as the documents in favour of complainant are dated 22.11.1997 and the forged documents are dated 07.11.1997, so this also clear indicates that the forged documents were prepared with the sole intention to cheat the complainant.

sentences.text: The appellant/accused by signing as Joginder Singh on Ex. P-4 to Ex. P-7 actively participated in the said criminal conspiracy.
Hence, it is crystal clear that the appellant/accused was a part of criminal conspiracy for preparation of forged property documents of the plot in question, so as to cheat the complainant.

So, he has been rightly convicted for the offence of criminal conspiracy u/s 120B IPC to cheat the complainant and also for entering into criminal conspiracy for forging documents Ex.
P-4 to P-7.
24.
As regards offence u/s 471 IPC is concerned, it is duly proved that the documents Ex. P-4 to P-7 are forged documents.
The said documents have been used before the Sub-Registrar as genuine documents for the purpose of its registration.

The appellant/accused was one of the fake executants of the said documents and he appeared before Sub-Registrar Kashmere Gate to get the same registered impersonating as Joginder Singh despite being fully aware of the fact that the documents were forged documents.
He also got the same registered by way of impersonation inducing a false belief with the Sub-Registrar that the documents were genuine documents.
So even offence u/s 471 IPC is clearly made out against the appellant/accused.

Infact in the considered opinion of this court,

25. The appellant has stated in his appeal that prosecution should have examined Sh. O.P. Sachdeva to prove the signature of PW-1.

However, when PW- 1 himself, was examined in court and he admitted his signatures on Ex. PW-1/A DOD : 04.01.2023 Page no. 12 of 14 Shyam Singh vs State CA No. 219//19 and PW-1/B, there was no need for the prosecution to examine Sh. O.P. Sachdeva.

sentences.text: As regards non production of property documents of the concerned plot by PW-1 is concerned, it is pertinent to mention that the same would have been material had the forged documents Ex. P-4 to P-7 had been executed by the appellant/ accused alongwith other co-accused persons in their individual capacity.

However, when they had signed the documents Ex. P-4 to P-7 by impersonating themselves as PW-1 and deceased Munshi Ram, the partners of the partnership firm M/s Sachdeva Industries, the actual owner of the plot in question, there was no requirement for the prosecution to prove that the plot was indeed in the name of PW-1 and Munshi Ram or not.
26.

It was also contended on behalf of appellant/accused that no payment was made by complainant to the appellant/accused nor complainant had seen him at any point of time at the time of entering into transaction and so there was no question of appellant/accused being involved in commission of any offence with the complainant.

Even this contention is not sustainable for the simple reason that the appellant/accused was not convicted by the Ld. Trial Court for the offence of Sec. 420 IPC but he has been convicted for the offence u/s 120B/468/471 IPC.

Moreover, in cases of criminal conspiracy,
the conspirators act in unison and different roles are assigned to different people which culminate in the ultimate commission of offence and so, it is not open for one of the conspirators to take the plea that any or some of the criminal acts attributed to the conspirators was not done by him individually.
Even otherwise, I have already discussed at length as to how the role of the appellant/accused is clearly made out in the present case in the foregoing paragraphs.
The other contentions raised in the appeal have already been discussed and are discarded.

sentences.text: In my considered opinion, there is no illegality, infirmity or impropriety in the judgment dated 28.09.2018 passed by Ld. Trial Court.
Infact the Ld. Trial Court rightly convicted the appellant for the offences punishable u/s 120B/468/471 IPC on the basis of evidence on record.
The appeal accordingly, stands dismissed qua the aforesaid judgment.
The Appellant be heard separately on the point of sentence.

PW1 also did not handover any document pertaining to the partnership firm M/s Sachdeva Industries.
Hence, there was no question that he could have signed documents on 07.11.1997 or could have appeared before the Sub Registrar later on for registration of those documents.
The knowledge of PW2 qua the signatures on Ex. P-4 to Ex.P- 7 is merely based on the information which he gathered from his local inquiry and not within his personal knowledge.
Hence, in view of the aforesaid, it is clearly proved that the appellant/accused had participated in forgery of the above documents by signing the same as Joginder Singh for the purpose of cheating and so offence u/s 468 IPC is duly proved against him.
Two persons impersonate themselves as the actual owners of one plot, out of which the appellant/accused impersonated as Joginder Singh and another co-accused Shiv Charan (since expired) impersonated himself as Munshi Ram (already expired 8 years ago from the date of execution of the documents Ex. P-4 to P-7) and they then executed GPA, Agreement to Sell, etc in favour of other co-accused Nanak Chand and even got it registered from the office of Sub- Registrar.
This was not possible until and unless there was a prior meeting of minds of the accused persons and them having hatched a criminal conspiracy to cheat the complainant.
The appellant/accused by signing as Joginder Singh on Ex. P-4 to Ex. P-7 actively participated in the said criminal conspiracy.
Hence, it is crystal clear that the appellant/accused was a part of criminal conspiracy for preparation of forged property documents of the plot in question, so as to cheat the complainant.
So, he has been rightly convicted for the offence of criminal conspiracy u/s 120B IPC to cheat the complainant and also for entering into criminal conspiracy for forging documents Ex.
P-4 to P-7.
24.
As regards offence u/s 471 IPC is concerned, it is duly proved that the documents Ex. P-4 to P-7 are forged documents.
The said documents have been used before the Sub-Registrar as genuine documents for the purpose of its registration.
The appellant/accused was one of the fake executants of the said documents and he appeared before Sub-Registrar Kashmere Gate to get the same registered impersonating as Joginder Singh despite being fully aware of the fact that the documents were forged documents.
He also got the same registered by way of impersonation inducing a false belief with the Sub-Registrar that the documents were genuine documents.
So even offence u/s 471 IPC is clearly made out against the appellant/accused.
even the offence u/s 419 IPC stands proved against the appellant/accused but he was not convicted for the same.
However, when they had signed the documents Ex. P-4 to P-7 by impersonating themselves as PW-1 and deceased Munshi Ram, the partners of the partnership firm M/s Sachdeva Industries, the actual owner of the plot in question, there was no requirement for the prosecution to prove that the plot was indeed in the name of PW-1 and Munshi Ram or not.
26.
Even this contention is not sustainable for the simple reason that the appellant/accused was not convicted by the Ld. Trial Court for the offence of Sec. 420 IPC but he has been convicted for the offence u/s 120B/468/471 IPC.
Moreover, in cases of criminal conspiracy,
the conspirators act in unison and different roles are assigned to different people which culminate in the ultimate commission of offence and so, it is not open for one of the conspirators to take the plea that any or some of the criminal acts attributed to the conspirators was not done by him individually.
